Legs.Subject: BinaryFields.Degree8/16/32/64/128's Degree and ReductionTail, read off the shipped fields row by row
Legs.Against: Subjects.BinaryFieldCatalogModuli — (8, 0x1B), (16, 0x2B), (32, 0x8D), (64, 0x1B), (128, 0x87)
Legs.Citation: the standard minimum-weight irreducible at each degree, tabulated in src/Puck.Maths/FiniteFields/README.md's BinaryFields table and outside this tree; Swan's theorem forbids a trinomial at every degree that is a multiple of eight, which every one of these is, so a weight-five pentanomial is the floor. The degree-64 tail COINCIDING with the degree-8 tail is the published pattern rather than a transcription error, and the pair is compared row by row so a copied row would fail

Legs.Subject: BinaryField<T>.Multiply at all five catalog fields, on operands folded to the field by Subjects.BinaryFieldElement
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldProduct at the PUBLISHED degree and tail — schoolbook carryless multiply into a double-width polynomial then bit-by-bit reduction from the top, in BigInteger. The published pair rather than the field's own readers is what makes a wrong catalog constant visible: read off the field, the same wrong tail would flow into both sides. EXACT on both sides — this wing rounds nowhere — so the substrate condition does not arise

Legs.Subject: BinaryField<T>.Multiply at a modulus DRAWN FROM THE OPERAND STREAM — a degree in [1, width] and an odd tail below t^degree, at every one of the five carriers
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldProduct at that same drawn pair. This is where the degree-below-the-carrier-width path is swept: the low mask built by right-shifting all-ones, the split at the degree and the iterated tail fold all behave differently there, and the catalog fields — every one of which has degree equal to its carrier's width — never reach it

Legs.Subject: BinaryField<T>.Reduce on an UNREDUCED carrier value at the drawn modulus, at every one of the five carriers
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldReduce — schoolbook long division against the modulus MATERIALIZED IN FULL, leading term included. The subject never materializes t^degree: it stores only the tail and folds the high part by multiplying it BY the tail. A dropped leading term, a Split that returned its value unshifted, or a fold loop unrolled to one pass all diverge here on the first drawn modulus that needs a second pass. ENVELOPE, measured rather than assumed: ReduceWide's low mask is deliberately built by right-shifting all-ones instead of as (1 << degree) − 1, and rebuilding it the second way is NOT falsifiable through the public surface, because Split short-circuits at degree == width and returns before the mask is read — the mutation is inert at every carrier. That construction is belt and braces rather than load bearing, and this law says so instead of implying it is pinned

Legs.Subject: IsReduced answers the raw's own high-bit test at every drawn degree and is unconditionally true where the degree equals the carrier's width; Reduce is the identity on an already-reduced element; and Reduce(t^degree) is exactly the ReductionTail wherever the degree leaves room for that value, which is the defining congruence the whole tail representation rests on. ENVELOPE: at degree == width the t^degree probe is unrepresentable in the carrier and is not made. ENVELOPE: in Domains.Vectors' single-lane edge phase every other lane is cleared, so a 128-bit operand assembled from two lanes carries a zero half there and the drawn modulus lands on degree 1, tail 1 — GF(2), which the wing builds on every cyclic-incidence run and is a real instantiation rather than a degenerate one

the field axioms hold BIT-FOR-BIT at all five carriers and at a modulus drawn from the operand stream: commutativity, associativity, distributivity, both identities, the annihilator, addition as its own inverse, Square as Multiply(a, a) — the wing's 'no separate squaring kernel on any tier' invariant stated as an observable — and Frobenius additivity, which is what licenses SquareRoot being repeated squaring. Everything here is EXACT: nothing rounds, saturates or approximates anywhere in the wing, so condition (B) does not arise at all — there is no rounding substrate for the two sides to share, and 'they agree because they round alike' is not a reading this statement admits

ENVELOPE, and it is the point of this case's shape: the axioms hold under ANY legal modulus, so agreement here pins the ARITHMETIC and never the modulus. A reduction that consistently used the wrong irreducible would satisfy every line above. What pins the modulus is binary-field.product-and-reduction-vs-oracle's published-constant and oracle legs and binary-field.irreducibility-vs-trial-division; this case is what catches a product wrong in a way no single oracle comparison would isolate — a non-associative fold, a distributivity break at a carry edge, an identity that moves at one degree
BinaryField<T>.Inverse at all five catalog fields
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldProduct(value, inverse) == 1 in BigInteger — a CERTIFICATE rather than a recomputation, and a complete one: a field has exactly one inverse per non-zero element, so the product being one identifies the answer uniquely. Reached without exponentiating anything, where the subject reaches it as value^(2^degree − 2). EXACT on both sides, so the substrate condition does not arise

Legs.Subject: BinaryField<T>.Inverse at the degree-8 and degree-16 catalog fields
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldInverse — the EXTENDED EUCLIDEAN almost-inverse loop over BigInteger polynomials, a wholly different derivation from the Itoh–Tsujii Frobenius addition chain the subject walks; its step budget's exhaustion is a NAMED failure naming the modulus rather than a spin. ENVELOPE: this second derivation runs at the two narrow catalog degrees at Default and at all five at deep.binary-field-multiplicative-group; at degrees 32, 64 and 128 the certificate leg above is what stands, and it is complete for the value even though it is not a second derivation of it

Legs.Subject: BinaryField<T>.Divide and BinaryField<T>.SquareRoot at all five catalog fields
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldProduct: the quotient re-multiplied by the divisor must return the dividend, and the root squared must return the argument, both in BigInteger. Stated as certificates rather than as Divide == Multiply(left, Inverse(right)) or SquareRoot == Degree − 1 squarings, either of which would transcribe the subject's own body and prove only that it was copied faithfully

Legs.Subject: BinaryField<T>.Exponentiate at the degree-8 catalog field over the CONTIGUOUS exponents zero through thirteen
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldRepeatedProduct — the SEQUENTIAL fold, one ordinary product per unit of exponent, against the subject's square-and-multiply walk over the exponent's binary expansion. Different schedules, so a mis-stepped square-and-multiply cannot agree by construction; contiguous rather than sparse because every exponent through thirteen exercises a different schedule and the fold costs one product per step either way. ENVELOPE: the fold runs at one degree and to thirteen at Default; deep.binary-field-multiplicative-group runs it at all five catalog degrees

Legs.Subject: Exponentiate at the multiplicative group order — value^(2^k − 1) == One and value^(2^k − 2) == Inverse(value) for every non-zero value at k = 8, 16, 32 and 64
Legs.Against: Subjects.BinaryFieldGroupOrders — 255, 65535, 4294967295, ulong.MaxValue
Legs.Citation: Lagrange's theorem: the multiplicative group of GF(2^k) has order 2^k − 1, so every non-zero element raised to it is the identity. The wing README states the degree-8 reading (Exponentiate(0x03, 255) == 1) for a structural reason rather than a coincidental one, and this leg is that reading generalized to every accelerated degree. ENVELOPE: degree 128 has NO row, because 2^128 − 1 does not fit the ulong exponent Exponentiate takes. The orders are WRITTEN OUT rather than computed as (1UL << k) − 1UL, whose shift count at k = 64 is masked back to zero in C#

Legs.Subject: Exponentiate(value, order − 1)
Legs.Against: Inverse(value), on the same operand, at four degrees
Legs.Shared: BinaryFieldKernels.Multiply — the IDENTICAL member, reached from Exponentiate's square-and-multiply loop (BinaryFieldKernels.cs:205,209) and from Inverse's addition chain (cs:239,248,259). Both sides are EXACT over GF(2), so condition (B) is vacuous: there is no rounding substrate to share
Legs.Citation: legs 1 and 2 of this same case pin Inverse independently in BigInteger on the same operand stream, and binary-field.product-and-reduction-vs-oracle pins Multiply against Oracles.BinaryFieldProduct at all five catalog degrees

Legs.Subject: Exponentiate(value, 0) is One at every swept operand and at Zero — the documented degenerate case, and the one a naive square-and-multiply gets wrong — and Inverse and Divide refuse a zero divisor with DivideByZeroException at all five carriers. The refusal ladder is a SEPARATE fixed claim running once per run rather than once per swept operand, and honestly so: both guards read only the divisor, so no dividend can change either answer, and a caught exception costs some forty microseconds that a per-operand ladder would spend four hundred times over for one bit of information. A zero divisor is substituted with one identically in subject and oracle so every sampled pair reaches a defined comparison; the zero DIVIDEND is not substituted and is swept, so Divide(0, w) == 0 falls to the certificate leg above

ScaleRegion, MultiplyAccumulateRegion and ScaleRegionInPlace at BinaryFields.Degree8 and BinaryFields.Degree16, over twenty lengths from zero through 259 crossed with four scalars — the annihilator, the identity, the ReductionTail (which makes the tail fold maximally active) and the densest element
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryFieldProduct element by element, in BigInteger. These are the ONLY two carriers the region-scaling ladder's vector rungs reach — byte-wide elements reach all seven rungs and sixteen-bit elements the three affine ones — so this is where a shared-nothing region expectation is worth paying for. Leg 2 of this same case builds its expectation from the field's OWN Multiply and says so (shared-substrate:delegation-twin), and binary-field.region-lengths-vs-scalar-rung compares one shipped rung against another; this leg is the one whose expectation is formed in BigInteger with the subject nowhere inside it, which is what makes it independent evidence rather than carriage

Legs.Subject: ScaleRegion, MultiplyAccumulateRegion and ScaleRegionInPlace at BinaryFields.Degree32, Degree64 and Degree128 over the same ladder
Legs.Against: the elementwise expectation built from the same field's Multiply
Legs.Shared: BinaryField<T>.Multiply — the identical member the region's own scalar rung calls (BinaryFieldKernels.cs:472,479). Carriage only: what this proves is the loop, the length arithmetic and the accumulate mask, never the product
Legs.Citation: leg 1 of this same case pins the region product classically at the two carriers that have a vector rung at all; at these three widths every length runs MultiplyAccumulateRegionScalar and nothing else, so there is no second implementation to disagree with. The first sixty-five indices additionally take the BigInteger oracle here — which covers every ladder length through 65 — so the wide carriers are not left on carriage alone

Legs.Subject: the aliasing contract, stated as arithmetic rather than as a permission: an exactly aliased ScaleRegion equals the in-place form; an exactly aliased MultiplyAccumulateRegion leaves Multiply(Add(One, scalar), value) at every index, which holds only if every rung loads its source before storing its destination at the same offset; AddRegion onto itself zeroes the region. A shifted overlap is refused with ArgumentException naming 'source', at all three validating members, and ScaleRegionInPlace validates nothing because it passes one span as both sides. Each length row additionally requires the element one past the region to be untouched

AddRegion is degree-independent, and it is stated where that is not vacuous: at a degree-9 field over the sixteen-bit carrier, on content that violates every OTHER region member's reduced-operand precondition by construction — the claim body counts the unreduced elements and fails if the ladder does not reach its own operand class. At a catalog field the statement would say nothing, because degree equals width there and every packed value is already reduced. It is the wing's one region member outside the scaling ladder, and this is the statement that would catch it acquiring a reduction

the length-mismatch refusal is an ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming the PUBLIC parameter 'source', at all three validating members and in BOTH directions of mismatch — a shorter source and a longer one — and it lands before anything is written: the eight-element buffer carries distinct content and every element is compared back after each refused call. The name is intentional rather than inherited: the refusal is thrown explicitly, because the throw helper it used to run captured the caller-argument expression of ValidateRegion's first argument and reported the literal string 'source.Length', which is a property expression and not a parameter of any public member. This statement REPLACES the doc gap that pinned that string; the three members' XML docs now name source, and the shifted-overlap refusal already did

the whole admission surface at all five carriers and five degrees each — degree one, degree two, half the width, one below the width and the width itself: Create succeeds, Degree and ReductionTail read back exactly what was passed, IsReduced answers correctly at One, at Zero, at the degree's all-ones mask and at t^degree, and Reduce(t^degree) is the ReductionTail. The degree == width row is the one the representation exists for: a degree-k modulus needs k + 1 bits and would not fit the carrier, which is why the leading term is implicit

the refusal ladder, each row asserting the exception TYPE and the ParamName: an unsupported carrier (char and nuint, both of which satisfy the IBinaryInteger/IUnsignedNumber constraint and neither of which is one of the five fixed widths — nuint is eight bytes wide on this target, so it would otherwise look exactly like ulong to CarrierBitCount) is refused with NotSupportedException BEFORE the degree is looked at; a degree below one or above the carrier's width names 'degree'; an even tail — a zero constant term, where t divides the modulus and the quotient is not a field — names 'reductionTail'; a tail with a coefficient at or above the degree names 'reductionTail', and that check is SKIPPED at degree == width, where nothing can sit above it. FromModulus refuses the zero polynomial and the degree-zero constant with ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming 'modulus' — the same shared range rule Create runs, asserted EXACTLY so the ArgumentException base cannot stand in — and its carrier check still precedes the degree rules, so an unsupported carrier reports NotSupportedException from both factories

FromModulus's two DERIVED refusals name 'modulus', the one parameter its caller supplied: a modulus whose degree exceeds the carrier's width throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming 'modulus', and a modulus with a zero constant term throws ArgumentException naming 'modulus'. The counterexample reads the offending name back rather than reporting a bare boolean. The same rows are what pins the two factories APART: Create's own degree and tail refusals still name 'degree' and 'reductionTail', so the shared validation core is reporting the name it was handed rather than one set of names having swallowed the other. This statement REPLACES the doc gap that pinned the leaked names; FromModulus's XML doc attributed both conditions to modulus all along, and the code now agrees with it
the five catalog fields' identity
Legs.Against: Create(8, 0x1B), Create(16, 0x2B), Create(32, 0x8D), Create(64, 0x1B), Create(128, 0x87), compared by record equality against BinaryFields.Degree8/16/32/64/128
Legs.Citation: the standard minimum-weight irreducibles at those degrees, tabulated in src/Puck.Maths/FiniteFields/README.md. The two top rows also carry a load-bearing structural fact: BinaryPolynomial's packed carrier tops out at degree 63, so Degree64 and Degree128 are reachable ONLY through Create, and the round-trip ladder below shows FromModulus reaching degree 63 and no further

Legs.Subject: FromModulus round-trips the leading-term strip: for a committed ladder of degrees through 63 with odd tails, FromModulus of (t^degree + tail) reports that degree and that tail exactly. ENVELOPE: BinaryPolynomial's own packed-bits constructor and Bits reader are INPUTS here rather than subjects — this case could not catch either of them being wrong, so neither is cited, and both answer to polynomial.additive-group-and-accessors

a DEFAULT-INITIALIZED field REFUSES its whole semantic surface with InvalidOperationException, at all five supported carriers and at an unassigned array element of each: One, Zero, Add, AddRegion, Divide, Exponentiate, Inverse, IsIrreducible, IsReduced, Multiply, MultiplyAccumulateRegion, Reduce, ScaleRegion, ScaleRegionInPlace, Square and SquareRoot, each named in the failure text so a member that quietly answers is reported as itself. Every one of these previously returned a PLAUSIBLE answer at degree zero — the truncated carryless product, an identity Reduce, an identity SquareRoot from a loop handed −1, and a successful Inverse(One) — none of which is arithmetic in GF(2^k). Degree and ReductionTail are deliberately outside the policy and still read zero, and this case asserts that the default value therefore stays comparable and that a CONSTRUCTED field is untouched: it answers, both identities read back, and record equality still reads the degree and the tail rather than any encoding of them. PRINTABILITY is asserted on ToString at both ends: a hand-written PrintMembers prints the degree and the tail alone, so a default value formats as its raw state instead of throwing from a guarded identity, and a constructed field renders no identity as if it were carried state

the same refusal at an UNSUPPORTED carrier: default(BinaryField<char>) refuses Multiply, Add, Inverse, IsIrreducible and One with the SAME InvalidOperationException. That carrier has no constructed state at all — Create rejects it with NotSupportedException before the degree is read — so the uninitialized diagnosis is the only thing its default value can say, and the policy makes it say exactly what the five supported carriers say rather than reaching degree-independent members undiagnosed
BinaryField<byte>.IsIrreducible at EVERY one of the 255 legal degree-1-through-8 moduli
Legs.Against: Oracles.BinaryPolynomialIsIrreducible — exhaustive trial division by every polynomial of degree one through half the modulus's own, in BigInteger. The definition against the Ben-Or/Rabin criterion: the subject squares the indeterminate degree times and takes gcds of t^(2^i) + t against the modulus through a bespoke first Euclid step that never materializes the modulus, and the oracle just divides. Exhaustive rather than sampled, so this is a TOTAL statement over that whole range and not a probe. EXACT on both sides, so the substrate condition does not arise

Legs.Subject: the count of constructible irreducible moduli the sweep above finds at each degree from one through eight
Legs.Against: Subjects.BinaryIrreducibleCounts — 2, 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, 30 — with the degree-one entry taken as one
Legs.Citation: OEIS A001037, the number of monic irreducible polynomials of each degree over GF(2) — Gauss's necklace count, an external property of the ring itself. The published degree-one entry is 2 and the sweep can only find 1, because t has a zero constant term and Create refuses it; every irreducible of degree two or above has a non-zero constant term, so those rows are the published values unchanged. An implementation that is self-consistently wrong still cannot reproduce a published property of GF(2)[t]. The table is the binary-polynomial family's own, reused rather than copied

Legs.Subject: IsIrreducible() at all five catalog fields
Legs.Against: true at every one
Legs.Citation: the standard minimum-weight irreducibles at degrees 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128, tabulated in src/Puck.Maths/FiniteFields/README.md. The catalog deliberately does NOT validate irreducibility at construction — the README says the constants are not trusted on their word and expect an external gate — and Post's binary-field stage re-proves the same five at run time

Legs.Subject: IsIrreducible() at t^degree + 1 for degree 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128
Legs.Against: false at every one
Legs.Citation: the Frobenius identity in characteristic two: t^(2^k) + 1 = (t + 1)^(2^k), so the modulus is a perfect power and maximally reducible. ENVELOPE: this is the ONLY negative statement this suite makes at degrees 32, 64 and 128 — the trial-division oracle's divisor space doubles with every degree and is out of reach above the teens, so the positive statement at the wide degrees rests on the published constants plus Post's binary-field stage, and deep.binary-field-irreducible-census is where the exhaustive agreement is carried further

Legs.Subject: ENVELOPE on a branch that cannot be falsified, measured rather than assumed: the kernel's closing `power == indeterminate` test — Rabin's t^(2^degree) ≡ t condition — is UNREACHABLE as a decision, because the loop above it runs the STRENGTHENED Ben-Or form over every exponent through half the degree, and every reducible modulus has an irreducible factor of degree at most half its own, so the greatest-common-divisor arm has already returned false by the time that test is read. Replacing it with a bare `true` moves no answer over the 255 moduli here or the 8190 the binary-polynomial family sweeps; the only legal degree-one modulus is t + 1, which is irreducible either way. This law pins the DECISION, not that closing guard, and says so rather than implying the guard is covered

BinaryField<T>.IsIrreducible at degrees 32, 64 and 128 — the Ben-Or/Rabin criterion in BinaryFieldKernels — on the catalog modulus at each degree and on the first FURTHER modulus the subject accepts there, taken over the 128-bit carrier
Legs.Against: an exact multiplicative-ORDER certificate in BigInteger: an element a of the quotient ring with a^(2^d − 1) = 1 and a^((2^d − 1)/p) not 1 at every prime p dividing 2^d − 1. Its order is then 2^d − 1 EXACTLY, so its powers are that many distinct units of a ring holding 2^d elements one of which is zero — every non-zero element therefore inverts, the quotient IS a field, and the modulus is irreducible. A COMPLETE proof and not a probe, and it shares nothing with the subject: no Frobenius exponentiation, no greatest common divisor, no carrier, no split, no reduction tail folded the subject's way — only Oracles.BinaryFieldProduct and a square-and-multiply schedule over BigInteger. This is the statement the wide degrees never had: trial division, the oracle every narrow irreducibility law answers to, has a divisor space that doubles with the degree and cannot be run at 32 at all
Legs.Citation: the prime divisors are the published Fermat-number factorizations, 2^32 + 1 = 641 x 6700417 and 2^64 + 1 = 274177 x 67280421310721; the catalog tails 0x8D, 0x1B and 0x87 are the standard minimum-weight irreducibles tabulated in src/Puck.Maths/FiniteFields/README.md. NEITHER is trusted here — the last structural leg of this case re-multiplies every factorization and re-proves every factor prime before a certificate reads it, and the tails are decided by the certificate rather than accepted

Legs.Subject: IsIrreducible at the same three degrees on moduli that are REDUCIBLE by construction — five shapes per degree: a linear factor against everything else, the balanced split (a perfect SQUARE, both factors being the same polynomial there), and three off-centre splits
Legs.Against: the construction itself. Each modulus is the carryless PRODUCT of two non-constant polynomials, formed by Oracles.CarrylessProduct in BigInteger, so the reference verdict follows from how the operand was built and no decision procedure is consulted anywhere. Before a row is used the claim body requires the product to have landed on the intended degree with a non-zero constant term, so a construction that silently degenerated reddens the case rather than emptying it. These are the first negative statements this suite makes at 32, 64 and 128 beyond the single perfect power t^d + 1, whose reducibility follows from the Frobenius identity and which is one operand

Legs.Subject: IsIrreducible at degrees 32 and 64 over the 128-bit carrier, where the degree sits strictly BELOW the carrier width — a different mask, a different split and a different fold from the degree == width case the five catalog fields alone reach
Legs.Against: the same decision at the same degree over its own uint or ulong carrier, at every modulus this case touches: the catalog tail, every scanned tail whether accepted or rejected, and every reducible construction
Legs.Shared: the irreducibility decision in BinaryFieldKernels — ONE generic body specialized at two widths, so agreement proves the width plumbing and never the criterion. Both sides are exact over GF(2), so condition (B) is vacuous: there is no rounding substrate to share
Legs.Citation: legs 1 and 2 of this same case, which pin the criterion itself at BOTH verdicts and at all three degrees against evidence that runs no decision at all

Legs.Subject: the ACCEPTING arm is exercised rather than merely available: the claim body counts the moduli the subject accepts per degree and fails below a floor of one. A subject that called every modulus reducible would satisfy the negative leg outright and leave the certificate leg quantified over nothing, and the counter is what makes that a red rather than a green

the certificate's own basis, re-derived rather than transcribed: each published prime list is multiplied back and required to equal 2^d − 1 exactly, and every listed factor is re-proved prime by trial division — up to 67280421310721, whose divisor scan reaches 8.2 million. A composite listed as prime would admit an element of SMALLER order to the certificate and quietly weaken every positive verdict in this case, so the check runs once before any certificate is taken

IsIrreducible over the first SIXTEEN THOUSAND odd tails at each of degrees 32, 64 and 128, with EVERY modulus the subject accepts certified rather than only the first — hundreds of accepting verdicts per degree where the Default sibling takes two
Legs.Against: the same exact multiplicative-ORDER certificate in BigInteger that binary-field.wide-degree-irreducibility-certificates uses, run once per accepted modulus. What scale buys here is the accepting arm: one wrong accept anywhere in the scanned band is a counterexample, where the Default sibling could only see it if it happened to fall on the catalog tail or the first accepted row
Legs.Citation: the same published Fermat-number factorizations, re-multiplied and re-proved prime in the body before any certificate reads them

Legs.Subject: IsIrreducible on sixty reducible-by-construction moduli per degree — the five factor shapes crossed with twelve interior coefficient patterns
Legs.Against: the construction: each is the carryless product of two non-constant polynomials formed in BigInteger, so the reference verdict is derived without the subject. The rejecting arm at twelve times the Default sibling's width

Legs.Subject: IsIrreducible at degrees 32 and 64 over the 128-bit carrier, at EVERY one of the sixteen thousand scanned tails and every construction
Legs.Against: the same decision over the degree's own uint or ulong carrier
Legs.Shared: the irreducibility decision in BinaryFieldKernels — one generic body specialized at two widths, so agreement proves the width plumbing and never the criterion; exact on both sides, so condition (B) is vacuous
Legs.Citation: legs 1 and 2 of this same case, and binary-field.wide-degree-irreducibility-certificates, which make the criterion's own statement

Legs.Subject: ENVELOPE, and it is a tier requirement rather than a stylistic one: this case consumes NO Domain. Its whole operand basis — the tail scan, the split ladder and the coefficient patterns — is written inline in the claim body, because an Exhaustive case that drew from a domain would advance the frontier counter its Default sibling reads and slide that sibling's operands as a side effect of a sweep having been run

the accepting arm carries a floor of EIGHT accepted moduli per degree here rather than the Default sibling's one, and the published factorizations are re-multiplied and re-proved prime by trial division before any certificate is taken, exactly as at Default
